In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of in-store marketing on consumer behavior.
understanding how consumers process information in the store and how this affects purchase behavior.
understanding the effects of in-store and out-of-store factors on consumers' brand attention and brand evaluations at the point of sale, and how these effects translate into actual brand choice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the number of facings and shelf position have a strong impact on consumer evaluation that is entirely driven by its effect on attention and works particularly for low market share products, frequent users, and young, highly educated consumers who trade off brand and product.
in store marketing works, but not always in a straightforward way.
the more facings a brand has on a shelf, the more likely consumers are to notice the brand, and the more they will like the brand.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in store marketing is not a silver bullet.
in store marketing can be effective in driving sales but only if the right conditions are in place.
in store attention is a necessary but not sufficient condition for in store sales.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the number of shelf facings can have a large effect on brand attention and evaluation, but that this effect is moderated by the position of the shelf.
in store marketing is not just about grabbing consumers' attention. Rather, it is about grabbing consumers' eyes in the right place, at the right time,
in store marketing is a powerful tool that should be used strategically to target the right consumers with the right products.
